shots.say: No rain for days and days! And Tumble is so, so thirsty.
I'm Milo! Can you help Tumble find a drink of water?
This is Tumble, the baby elephant. And this is his mama.
The water hole is dry, little one. We need the rain.
I will find water, Mama. One big, cool drink!
But where is the water, when there is no rain?
Follow your nose, Tumble. And stay close to Milo.
Off they go, to look for water.
Friends help friends, come along with me! Step by step, what will we see?
Here is the water hole. But, oh! Where is the water?
No water. Only dry, cracked mud.
Oh no. The water is all gone.
Is there any water in the water hole? Yes, or no?
My mouth is so dry, Milo. What can I do?
Tumble, you have a super nose. Your trunk!
An elephant can smell water with its trunk, from far, far away.
Sniff, sniff, sniff. I smell water! This way!
Can you sniff like Tumble? Sniff, sniff, sniff!
Tumble follows his nose. Over the hill, and past the tall, dry grass.
Under the big tree, somebody calls. Cheep, cheep, cheep!
Three little birds! Pip, Kiki and Bo.
We are thirsty, too. Our puddle is all dry.
And our wings are too tired to fly far.
Come with me! My nose can find water.
Tumble walks on. The birds hop after him. Hop, hop, hop. Too slow!
How can three little birds come along? Ride on Tumble, or stay here?
I know! Hop on my back, little birds!
Hop, hop, hop! Three birds on one elephant.
Thank you, Tumble! This is a very good seat.
And off they go. Sniff, sniff, sniff.
The smell stops at a pile of big rocks. Is the water here?
Look! Down in a crack, one small pool of water.
Water! Me first, me first!
Pip leans down. But the pool is too deep for a little beak.
I cannot reach it. Not even on my tiptoes!
So close. But we cannot get a drink.
Who has a long, long nose to reach the water? Tumble, or Pip?
My trunk is long. I can reach!
Tumble dips his trunk in. Slurp! He sucks the water up.
An elephant sucks water up its trunk. Then it blows the water into its mouth.
But now the little pool is empty. That was the last drink.
The water is in Tumble's trunk. And Tumble is so, so thirsty.
Three little birds look up at him. They are thirsty, too.
If I drink it all, my friends get nothing.
Oh, Milo. I do not know what to do.
What should Tumble do? Drink it all, or share?
I know. Friends help friends. I will share!
Tumble lifts his trunk. Open your beaks, little birds!
Squirt! A drink for Pip.
Squirt! A drink for Kiki.
Squirt! And a drink for Bo.
And the last three drops? Drip, drip, drip. Those are for Tumble.
How many birds got a drink? Count with me! One, two, three!
It was only a tiny sip. But I feel so happy inside.
Tweet, tweet, tweet! Thank you, Tumble!
Now we can fly again. And look what I see!
Up in the sky, big gray clouds are coming.
Rain is coming, Tumble! Rain!
Drip. Drop. Splash! Down comes the rain.
The little pool fills up. Up, up, up, to the very top.
Now I can have my big, cool drink. Slurp!
Tumble drinks and drinks. Glug, glug, glug.
Elephants squirt water over their bodies to keep cool.
The birds splash in the puddles. Splish, splash, splosh!
Back at the zoo, the rain has stopped. And Mama is waiting.
Mama! I found water. And I found three new friends!
Tumble gave us his last drink!
You shared, even when you were thirsty. I am so proud of you.
Mama wraps her trunk around Tumble. A big, warm trunk hug.
When we share, everybody feels good inside.
Do you remember? What does an elephant use to smell water? Its trunk, or its tail?
And where does an elephant blow the water? Into its mouth, or into its ear?
Friends help friends. Hooray, hooray! What a rainy, happy day!
See you on the next adventure, friends!
